decisions.claim: The filed hypothesis is upheld in full, and the half it left open -- 'whether the +8 entries come from call targets, from a prologue matcher, or from the ELF reader' -- resolves to CALL TARGETS in the Listing walk's function worklist, and nothing else.
decisions.evidence: `kuna xrefs plt_ppc64le --to 0x948` reports exactly one reference, `0x5f4 call _init+0x34  bl 0x948`, and the same for 0x6f8 (from 0x87c), 0x7c8 (from 0xa14) and 0x8b8 (from 0x5ec). Ablation pins the producer: `--option funcstart_patterns off`, `--option aif off` and `--option listing off` each leave all four entries in place, while `listing off` PLUS `fast_funcdisc off` removes them -- and both of those consumers commit `listing.functions()`, which only the walk fills. The ELF reader is excluded directly: no relocation, no `.eh_frame` FDE and no `.ctors`/`.dtors`/`.data.rel.ro` pointer in the image names a +8 address (`readelf -r`, `readelf --debug-dump=frames-interp`, `objdump -s`).

decisions.claim: `register_tm_clones` carries the identical `[<localentry>: 8]` annotation and is NOT split, which is what rules the prologue-matcher diagnosis out rather than merely making the call-target one plausible.
decisions.evidence: The only reference to its local entry 0x758 is `frame_dummy`'s tail branch (`0x8b8 jump  b 0x758`), not a `bl`. The walk mints a function at CALL targets and treats every other flow target as a same-function successor, so 0x758 never becomes an entry while 0x6f8/0x7c8/0x8b8/0x948 -- all four reached by `bl` -- do. A prologue or ELF-reader source would have produced 0x758 too.

decisions.claim: The need's warning that `--option ... off` on this path 'appears' not to take effect has a mundane cause and is not a precedence bug: `kuna functions` accepts no `--option` at all.
decisions.evidence: `kuna functions <binary> [--json] [--mode ...] [--define-function ...]` is the whole grammar (`kuna --help`); the discovery bundle is injected by `driver_default_options` and there is no user override on that surface. Driving the same ablations through `decompile-all`, which does take `--option`, makes every one of them take effect -- that is how the producer above was isolated.

decisions.claim: The fold is applied at the walk's CALL-target seam rather than as a post-hoc filter over committed entries, so the Listing's own function model is right too.
decisions.evidence: A post-hoc filter over `AnalysisOutput::entries` (the shape `fdeinterior` uses for FDE bodies) would have closed the probe, but `Listing::function_containing`, the region-containment guards in `tailcallentry` and the `aif` gap walk would all still believe 0x948 is a function. Gating one line above `unmappedentry` in `walk.rs` -- the sibling gate at the identical seam -- makes every consumer see one consistent model, and it is also strictly upstream of `funcdisc_recursive` AND `fast_funcdisc`, the two consumers the ablation identified.

decisions.claim: The fold is provably non-destructive, by wiring rather than by heuristic: it can only ever remove a duplicate second entry over a body that is walked either way.
decisions.evidence: Guard 4 admits a fold only when the GLOBAL entry is itself a walk seed with no other seed between the two, so the local entry's bytes are reached as that seed's fall-through whatever the fold does -- the walk's instruction closure is invariant. The third cargo test asserts the observable form of this on the fixture: exactly the four local-entry twins are removed, nothing is added, and no surviving function shrinks.

decisions.claim: `--option ppclocalentry off` restores the pre-change discovery set and emitted C byte for byte.
decisions.evidence: Whole-binary `decompile-all` on plt_ppc64le with the option off `diff`s clean against the same command run at base commit e3db5512. The two-pass cargo test drives the same two arms through the console and asserts the husk/twin sizes on the off arm.

decisions.claim: plt_ppc64le is the ONLY PowerPC binary anywhere in the tree, so the in-repo blast radius is one image, and it was swept whole-binary rather than at the witness alone.
decisions.evidence: A `file(1)` sweep over every non-source file in the repo finds one PowerPC image. Whole-binary `decompile-all` before/after: 19 entries -> 15; the four husks and their four anonymous twins collapse into four correctly-sized functions (deregister_tm_clones 8->96, __do_global_dtors_aux 8->240, frame_dummy 8->12, __do_global_ctors_aux 8->120, each matching objdump); every funcboundflow truncation warning in the image is gone. One non-obvious hunk was classified rather than waved through: __do_global_dtors_aux's TOC displacements change base from `v1 + -0x7ef0` (an opaque r2) to `v2 + 0x1f850` (r12 followed through the now-included `addis r2,r12,2; addi r2,r2,30528` TOC setup). Same address -- r2 = r12 + 0x27740, so r2 - 0x7ef0 == r12 + 0x1f850.

decisions.claim: A call site to a folded local entry still renders as `sub_6f8()`, a generated name for an address no longer in the inventory. Recorded, not hidden, and deliberately left out of scope.
decisions.evidence: Naming it after its enclosing function is a call-resolution change in kuna-decomp, a second mechanism in a different crate from the discovery fold -- and kuna's function symbols carry no extent (the gap `fdeinterior` documents), so there is no cheap 'which function contains this address' answer to hang it on. It is strictly smaller than the defect fixed: before this PR the body itself was unreachable under its real name. The same follow-up would give `kuna xrefs --to <named function>` its intra-module callers back.

decisions.claim: This ships with a cross-crate cargo test instead of a `tests/stages/` two-pass XML, because the stages corpus structurally cannot carry the defect.
decisions.evidence: Both parity corpora are symbol-less `<binaryimage>` bytechunks; the fold reads the ELF symbol table's `st_other` field, which no bytechunk has. The precedent is `noreturn_propagate`, which shipped covered by a cross-crate e2e for the same reason. `kuna-console/tests/verify_ppclocalentry.rs` runs both passes through `bootstrap_from_object` + `commit_pending_analysis` and IS run by `make rust-test`; `tests/cli/ppc64-localentry-splits-function.json` carries the promoted acceptance.

decisions.claim: Shipped default-ON (DIV-107). The acceptance probe runs `kuna decompile BIN __do_global_ctors_aux` with no options, so only default output can close the need -- and the flip is evidence-backed rather than asserted.
decisions.evidence: 0/675 datatest assertions and 0/603 stage assertions move (both PARITY OK, docs/baseline.json untouched), because the fold is architecture-gated to PPC64 and both corpora are x86-family bytechunks. It is a strict correction rather than a judgement -- the ABI defines the two entries as the same routine -- and it is bounded by four guards, so the option exists as an ablation lever, not because the rule is a guess.

decisions.claim: The speed budget is met, and the honest reading needs the on-vs-on control: on this box a short decompile's noise floor is wider than the budget.
decisions.evidence: Interleaved off/on min-of-25 on a PROVABLY inert x86-64 target (the architecture check returns an empty map before any per-seed work) measures -0.97% median against an on-vs-on control of +0.02% median; the MINIMUM statistic on the same identical-work control swings +23.43%, so minima are unusable here and medians are reported. The witness measures +8.80% median (control +0.34%), which is the cost of decompiling a recovered 120-byte body where the off arm decompiled an empty husk -- more work done, not overhead added.

speed_note: interleaved off/on, 25 rounds, median, on a provably inert x86-64 target (fauxware main); on-vs-on control on the same target is +0.02% median. The witness (plt_ppc64le __do_global_ctors_aux) measures +8.80% median with a +0.34% control -- its on arm decompiles a 120-byte recovered body where the off arm decompiled an empty husk.
